title: AA-P10-LIVE development smoke LS-01 (positive_control); source text from study-forensics-033
prompt: In a randomized study, elementary school students who received the weekly supplementary literacy instruction had better reading proficiency than students who received regular instruction.
context: A large-scale study investigated a literacy support program in which elementary school students received weekly supplementary instruction over two school years. Students were randomly assigned to either the program or regular instruction. By the end of the first year, participants' reading proficiency was on average two and a half months ahead of the comparison group, and this advantage was still detectable 26 months later. The researchers note that the effect remained stable across all age groups and that no systematic disadvantages were observed.
